claim_text: Balanced RPC F(1;1;1) equals the VCS objective J in value and gradient
assumptions: same critic class; same tensor and weights
allowed_conclusion: J is the balanced RPC objective (inherited objective)

claim_text: J(T) - S = -E_M(T - eta)^2; so J(T) <= S for every bounded T
assumptions: population expectation under the mixture M
prior_work: composite losses / Bregman increments (Reid and Williamson 2010)
allowed_conclusion: J is a population lower bound and second order in the critic error
not_implied: that an evaluated J-hat is a per-run lower bound

claim_text: Image (base-unit) count differs from pair count: K negatives per anchor are not K independent units
assumptions: fixed critic; i.i.d. base units
allowed_conclusion: valid uncertainty for shared-base pairs once checked

claim_text: On the registered partner (product negatives; same N joint + N product units) VCS has lower posterior MSE on S than S-KDE / Nystrom / RFF on every axis and than RuLSIF-tanh on 4 of 5 axes (on par on sample size: RuLSIF-tanh lower at N <= 1024)
assumptions: 3 synthetic generators; d_total <= 100; N <= 16384; 2000 updates; 3 seeds; rule 1 of P85
prior_work: RuLSIF (Yamada et al.); kernel density-ratio estimation
experiment: P85 / P86 rows re-read in R4-02 section 2
allowed_conclusion: VCS beats these same-target kernel estimators on equal data in these settings
not_implied: superiority at every N; superiority over matched JS; any image-data claim

claim_text: K = 8 cyclic or in-batch negatives lower the neural posterior MSE by 30-60 % vs product negatives for both VCS and JS at the same N (no extra data; 3.3x fit time or 17x memory)
assumptions: P85 grid; same N joint units; equal updates
allowed_conclusion: a pair-construction effect shared by both losses
not_implied: a property of the VCS loss; equivalence of extra pairs to extra independent samples

claim_text: Matched JS posterior MSE <= VCS in 42 of 45 ladder cells (5-25 % lower in most P85 cells; VCS better only at d_total 100)
assumptions: same network; pairs; lr grid and SELECT
prior_work: Deep InfoMax JS; balanced logistic loss
allowed_conclusion: matched JS is at least as accurate on S in these settings
not_implied: that JS is theoretically always better

claim_text: The squared plug-in of the same fitted critic reads S more accurately than J-hat: smaller |bias| in 70/72 and smaller RMSE in 69/72 cells
assumptions: 3 generators; N <= 16384; <= 4000 updates; VCS and JS fit losses
allowed_conclusion: the plug-in is the better point readout of S here
not_implied: results beyond these generators and budgets; that J is not useful as a training objective

claim_text: J-hat on EVAL is a valid (guaranteed) lower readout of S in every run
assumptions: none
allowed_conclusion: a negative seed-mean bias was observed in 72/72 cells (descriptive)
not_implied: a per-run guarantee (that needs a held-out concentration interval)

claim_text: Some cell reaches |J - S| <= 0.02 within 4000 updates
assumptions: the pre-set tolerance
allowed_conclusion: no tested budget reaches the tolerance
not_implied: that the tolerance is unreachable with more data or updates

claim_text: In-batch InfoNCE resolves adjacent dependence levels 1.3-6x more finely than VCS or JS; bounded S is not uniquely resolving on the synthetic ladders
assumptions: cross-target rule 5 (ordering probability; |delta| / sd); EVAL bound log 1024
prior_work: InfoNCE (van den Oord et al.); MINE; NWJ; SMILE
experiment: P86 rule 5; P151 section 3; SMILE addendum
allowed_conclusion: MI estimators resolve these ladders at least as finely

claim_text: VCS has lower variance than the MI estimators
assumptions: none
allowed_conclusion: VCS and JS both have small seed and evaluation spread on S
not_implied: a cross-target variance ranking (wording W7 is forbidden)

claim_text: The classical kernel CS plug-in with the median-heuristic bandwidth reads <= 13 % of its own truth at d = 20
assumptions: CS-IB bandwidth convention; multiples 0.25-2
allowed_conclusion: not a quantitative estimator at these dimensions
not_implied: anything about other bandwidth rules or low dimension

claim_text: Under contamination VCS's posterior error degrades less than JS's
assumptions: same target (contaminated posterior); same seed and construction; 3 seeds; descriptive t intervals
allowed_conclusion: VCS degrades less in 9/48 cells (mostly independent-pair contamination at eps 0.10-0.20); JS has the lower absolute error in 19/48 (VCS in none)
not_implied: noise robustness of VCS; the P134 title R1 supported as a current conclusion

claim_text: The VCS-based conditional dependence test has power >= the controls (T1)
assumptions: frozen SSL encoders; R = 100; informative cells
allowed_conclusion: T1 holds by its rule; the advantage comes from the exact closed-form linear critic and VAL selection
not_implied: that the J objective itself gives more power (vcs2 <= js2; js_exact >= vcs_closed in 8/9)

claim_text: The final VCS recipe (4 views; 800 ep) reaches 87.01 +- 0.53 on the selection split and 86.65 +- 0.26 on the official test (3 seeds)
assumptions: CIFAR-10; ResNet-18; frozen linear probe
allowed_conclusion: the 8x VCS recipe number

claim_text: At VCS's view / batch / epoch knobs the SimCLR and VICReg recipes exceed the VCS recipe at every compute point (SimCLR test +3.96 at 1x to +1.48 at 8x)
assumptions: P41 matched-knob search (12 single-seed units then 3 seeds)
prior_work: SimCLR (Chen et al. 2020); VICReg (Bardes et al. 2022)
allowed_conclusion: the controls lead the frozen VCS recipe at equal views and epochs

claim_text: SimCLR was tuned (tuned SimCLR; equal tuning budgets)
assumptions: none
experiment: P41 knob list; owner rule 2026-10-04 (P128 withdrawn)
allowed_conclusion: SimCLR recipe (tau 0.2; AdamW 1e-3) at VCS's view / epoch budget (P41)
not_implied: any SimCLR hyper-parameter search beyond P41's knobs; tuned-vs-tuned statements

claim_text: A-P3 (fixed (2;-1) scorer; all-view pairs; full negative gradient) 89.02 +- 0.04 vs SimCLR recipe 88.31 +- 0.21: linear +0.72 [+0.48; +0.95] over 5 seeds; kNN -0.45 [-0.92; +0.02]

allowed_conclusion: A-P3 exceeds the SimCLR recipe on the linear probe at equal views and epochs on the CIFAR-10 selection split

claim_text: VCS gains more from strong augmentation than SimCLR

claim_text: On CIFAR-100 the VCS family orders above SimCLR

allowed_conclusion: A-P3 = recipe (60.00 vs 59.91); vs SimCLR linear +1.75 but kNN -1.41: readouts disagree

claim_text: VCS's advantage over matched JS is tied to the shared default scorer
assumptions: matched JS on the same scorer (P114 / P120) and tuned grids for both (P129)
allowed_conclusion: C10 A-P3 - JS +0.21 (close); C100 +0.80 (clear; 5 seeds); tuned vs tuned: C10 close; C100 JS ahead -0.49 (lr-dependent)

claim_text: Under solo-learn's recipe VCS is within 1.5 points of SimCLR

claim_text: At ResNet-50 on CIFAR-100 A-P3 exceeds the SimCLR recipe: linear +5.17 [+2.68; +7.67]; kNN -1.59 [-3.25; +0.08]
assumptions: untuned SimCLR recipe; 3 seeds; seeds 1-2 added after seed 0

claim_text: VCS matches SimCLR on ImageNet-100 (pilot)
